summary: Cosmocraft is an interactive 3D satellite design and mission-planning simulator that helps players understand the engineering challenges of designing and developing spacecraft for real-world missions. Our project allows users to take on the role of satellite engineers by selecting a specific mission, designing satellites, managing finances and preparing them for launch. Players customize essential satellite components such as launch vehicles, spacecraft buses, propulsion systems, solar arrays, and optical cameras. They must also consider mass limits, power requirements, delta-v and mission budgets. Each mission presents different scientific objectives, ranging from monitoring Earth's climate and mapping it's surface to studying polar weather, exploring lunar ice and investigating Mars. By combining realistic engineering requirements with interactive 3D visualization, cosmo craft transforms complex aerospace concepts into an accessible learning experience, helping users understand the science, technology and decision-making behind successful space missions regardless of their financial barriers, physical limitations and limited access to space technology.
details:
CosmoCraft’s Project Solution

CosmoCraft is a browser-based 3D space mission simulator where players design their own satellite, choose a mission, and watch it work in orbit. It turns satellite engineering into an interactive, hands-on experience that anyone can try without installing anything.A scoring system rewards mission success, scientific value, efficient use of resources, and effective decision making.

How Does Our Solution Work

Players start by choosing a mission, [e.g. Earth observation, communication, weather], then build a satellite by selecting components. They launch it into a 3D environment and see how their design choices affect the mission.

  • Step 1: Choose a mission.
  • Players choose the type of satellite they are going to build. This gives the opportunity to observe changes in the satellites according to their functions
  • Step 2: Build the satellite.
    Players now need to build their own satellite. They can learn the consequences of changing the size/functionality of each component by changing them. when they reach th elimit they recieve an alert sign which gives them the opportunity to experience real-life difficulties.
  • Step 3: Launch and simulate. players will be engaged in launch campaign by pressing the buttons in green spot
  • players can observe the objects and send to earth. this simulation can make the players feel more like an astranaut
  • Furthermore, players will face space emergencies and make important choices to survive
  • Step 4: Results and learning. players will be scored according to how they launched and how easily they survived. these scores willdetermine their place in leaderboard

The Project Benefits

Students, educators, and space enthusiasts by:

  • Teaching how real satellites are designed and why each component matters.
  • Making space science accessible and fun through hands-on experimentation.
  • The game provides several orbital options and explain their basic characteristics.(Fron NASA's provided data)

Our Goal

To inspire the next generation of space engineers by letting anyone experience satellite mission design. One limitation that needs to be improved that players cannot players can not compete.
